option_description: Attestation that every remote-access session crossing this boundary (VPN tunnel, bastion login, ZTNA grant) requires multi-factor authentication before the session is established — no password-only path, no bypass groups, no single-factor fallback.
security_impact: References "Single-factor remote authentication at boundary" — its sole OR-condition — firing when mfa_enforced_at_boundary_crossing is false (T1078 Valid Accounts, T1133 External Remote Services, T1110 Brute Force). With MFA absent at the trust edge, a credential-stuffed or phished password yields a full tunnel into the trusted zone.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review the identity-provider / VPN concentrator authentication policy bound to the remote-access app: confirm MFA is required on every path, with no bypass group and no password-only fallback.
how_to_obtain.navigation: IdP admin console -> Authentication policies -> Application bound to VPN/bastion -> Required factors
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Policy shows MFA required for the remote-access app; no bypass groups, no password-only fallback.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Attempt VPN/bastion login with only username and password from an unenrolled client; observe whether the session is refused before tunnel establishment.
how_to_obtain.command: Attempt VPN/bastion login with only username+password from an unenrolled client; expect rejection or MFA challenge before tunnel/session is established.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Authentication fails or prompts a second factor; no session is granted on password alone.
how_to_obtain.source: NSA/CISA Selecting and Hardening Standards-based Remote Access VPN Solutions

how_to_obtain.instruction: Interview the IAM/remote-access team for the documented break-glass procedure and verify break-glass accounts still require a phishing-resistant factor (or are tightly monitored, time-bound, and alarmed) rather than being a hidden password-only path.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Break-glass accounts documented, tied to a strong factor, monitored with alerting on use; no quiet password-only side door.

option_description: Attestation that the remote-access boundary (VPN/bastion/ZTNA portal) accepts only phishing-resistant authenticators — FIDO2/WebAuthn security keys or PKI smartcards (PIV/CAC) — for the second factor. SMS, voice, email OTP, and push-only methods are disabled for this app.
security_impact: References "Phishable MFA factor (SMS/TOTP/push) on VPN portal" — its sole OR-condition — firing when phishing_resistant_authenticator_required is false (T1557 Adversary-in-the-Middle). Non-domain-bound factors can be relayed in real time by an AiTM proxy, yielding a working VPN session token despite MFA.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect the IdP authentication-methods policy bound to the VPN/bastion application: confirm only FIDO2/WebAuthn or PIV/CAC are permitted and that SMS, voice, email OTP, and push-only methods are explicitly disabled for this app.
how_to_obtain.navigation: IdP admin console -> Authentication methods -> Policy attached to VPN/bastion app -> Allowed authenticators
how_to_obtain.expected_output: IdP policy for the VPN/bastion app permits only FIDO2/WebAuthn or PIV/CAC; SMS, voice, email OTP, and push-only methods are disabled for this app.
how_to_obtain.source: CISA Implementing Phishing-Resistant MFA fact sheet

how_to_obtain.instruction: From a controlled test, attempt sign-in to a look-alike phishing origin proxying the real VPN portal and observe whether the FIDO2 authenticator refuses to assert.
how_to_obtain.command: Attempt sign-in to a look-alike phishing origin proxying the real VPN portal; expect the FIDO2 authenticator to refuse to assert because origin does not match.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Authenticator returns no assertion / browser surfaces origin mismatch; no credential leaves the device.
how_to_obtain.source: CISA Implementing Phishing-Resistant MFA fact sheet

how_to_obtain.instruction: Attempt to enrol a phishable factor (SMS, voice OTP, push-only) against the VPN/bastion app and confirm the IdP refuses the enrolment for this boundary.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Enrolment refused for this app; user-facing message indicates the factor is not permitted.

option_description: Attestation that the remote-access tunnel negotiates only a modern, NIST-recommended VPN protocol — WireGuard, IKEv2/IPsec with strong suites, or TLS-based SSL VPN with current TLS (>=1.2, preferably 1.3). Legacy protocols (PPTP, bare L2TP without IPsec, IKEv1 aggressive-mode PSK, SSLv2/SSLv3) are disabled and not negotiable.
security_impact: References "Weak or legacy VPN protocol and cipher suite" — one of its two OR-conditions — firing when vpn_protocol_modern_strong is false (T1040 Network Sniffing, T1562.010 Downgrade Attack). Legacy protocols permit offline cracking, downgrade, and MITM of the encrypted crossing.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect the VPN concentrator configuration for the list of enabled protocols and tunnel-group / connection-profile definitions.
how_to_obtain.command: Inspect VPN concentrator config: enabled protocols / tunnel-group definitions.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Only IKEv2/IPsec (per NIST SP 800-77r1) or modern TLS-based SSL VPN (per NIST SP 800-113) enabled; PPTP/L2TP-bare/SSLv2/SSLv3/TLS<1.2 absent.
how_to_obtain.source: NIST SP 800-77r1 Guide to IPsec VPNs

how_to_obtain.instruction: From an internet-side host, port-scan the VPN edge for the canonical VPN protocol ports and confirm legacy protocols do not answer.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Only sanctioned ports/protocols respond; 1723/tcp (PPTP) closed/absent.
how_to_obtain.source: NSA/CISA Selecting and Hardening Standards-based Remote Access VPN Solutions

how_to_obtain.instruction: Enumerate IKE proposals on the IPsec edge to confirm IKEv1 aggressive mode (and PSK paths) are not selectable.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: No IKEv1 aggressive-mode handshake; only IKEv2 proposals returned.
how_to_obtain.source: NIST SP 800-113 Guide to SSL VPNs

option_description: Attestation that the tunnel's negotiable cryptographic proposals include only NIST-approved suites for key exchange, encryption, and integrity — ECDH P-256+ or X25519 for KEX, AES-GCM-128/256 for confidentiality, SHA-256+ for integrity. Weak/legacy primitives (DES, 3DES, RC4, MD5, SHA-1, anon-DH, export-grade) are absent from IKE/IPsec proposals, OpenVPN cipher/tls-cipher lists, and TLS suite lists.
security_impact: References "Weak or legacy VPN protocol and cipher suite" — one of its two OR-conditions — firing when vpn_cipher_suites_strong_only is false (T1040 Network Sniffing, T1562.010 Downgrade Attack). Weak suites enable downgrade and offline cryptanalysis of the tunnelled traffic.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Read the IKE/IPsec proposal configuration (e.g. crypto ikev2 proposal stanzas, wg show, or openvpn server.conf 'cipher' / 'tls-cipher' directives).
how_to_obtain.command: Read IKE/IPsec proposal config (e.g. crypto ikev2 proposal / wg show / openvpn server.conf 'cipher','tls-cipher').
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Proposals list only NIST-approved suites; no DES, 3DES, MD5, SHA-1, RC4, anon-DH, or export-grade.
how_to_obtain.source: NIST SP 800-77r1 Guide to IPsec VPNs

how_to_obtain.instruction: Probe the SSL VPN edge with testssl.sh (TLS) and the IPsec edge with ike-scan -M to enumerate every negotiable suite.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: No weak/legacy suite negotiable; handshake fails for deprecated proposals.
how_to_obtain.source: NIST SP 800-113 Guide to SSL VPNs

how_to_obtain.instruction: If a bastion is in scope, enumerate the SSH KEX, cipher, and MAC algorithms it offers.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Only modern algorithms (chacha20-poly1305, aes256-gcm, curve25519-sha256, ssh-ed25519); no CBC, hmac-md5, sha1, or deprecated DH groups.
how_to_obtain.source: OpenSSH bastion / jump host hardening practice

option_description: Interpreted attestation that the remote-access channel forces all client traffic — including DNS — through the VPN tunnel (full-tunnel mode, default route 0.0.0.0/0 and ::/0 pushed, corporate DNS pushed, no split-include/exclude routes for internet ranges). True iff there is no parallel cleartext egress path on the VPN-connected device.
security_impact: References "Split-tunnel DNS / traffic leak bridging trust zones" — its sole OR-condition — firing when split_tunnel_disabled is false (T1572 Protocol Tunneling). A parallel cleartext egress on the VPN-connected host becomes an uncontrolled channel an adversary can pivot through, bridging untrusted-to-trusted.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Read the VPN client profile / connection profile and inspect the routes and DNS directives pushed to clients.
how_to_obtain.command: Read VPN client profile: routes pushed, dns directives.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Default route (0.0.0.0/0 and ::/0) pushed; DNS servers pushed; no split-include/exclude routes for internet ranges.
how_to_obtain.source: NSA/CISA Selecting and Hardening Standards-based Remote Access VPN Solutions

how_to_obtain.instruction: From a connected client, prove every hop traverses the VPN gateway and DNS resolution uses the corporate resolver, not the local ISP.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: All hops traverse VPN gateway; resolver address belongs to the corporate VPN, not the local ISP.
how_to_obtain.source: CISA Telework Reference Materials / Capacity Considerations

how_to_obtain.instruction: On a connected client, dump the effective routing table and confirm a single default route via the tunnel interface, with no parallel default through the physical NIC.
how_to_obtain.command: route print  # Windows -- or: ip route show  # Linux
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Default route points through the tunnel adapter; no competing 0.0.0.0/0 via the local NIC.

option_description: Attestation that before the remote-access session is established, the policy enforcement point evaluates endpoint health signals — patch level, EDR/AV running and healthy, disk encryption on, OS within supported baseline — as a hard precondition; non-compliant devices are denied or quarantined.
security_impact: References "No device posture / endpoint health attestation" — one of its two OR-conditions — firing when admin_endpoint_health_attested_at_elevation is false (T1133 External Remote Services). Without a posture verdict, a malware-infected or unmanaged endpoint terminates the tunnel and pivots into the trusted zone.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review the ZTNA / VPN conditional-access policy and confirm device-health signals (patch level, EDR healthy, FDE on, supported OS baseline) are evaluated as a hard precondition.
how_to_obtain.navigation: ZTNA / Conditional-Access admin console -> Policy for VPN/bastion app -> Device conditions
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Policy references a device-trust signal (managed cert, MDM compliance, EDR health) as a hard precondition; non-compliant devices are denied or quarantined.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Attempt connection from a deliberately non-compliant test device (out-of-date OS, EDR stopped, FDE off) with valid user MFA and observe whether admission is denied or quarantined.
how_to_obtain.command: Connect from an unmanaged / non-compliant device with valid user MFA; expect denial or quarantine VLAN.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Session denied or routed to remediation; trusted-zone resources unreachable.

option_description: Attestation that the remote-access boundary requires a managed-device claim (MDM/UEM enrollment, corporate device certificate, or equivalent attested device identity) before granting the tunnel/session; unenrolled or BYOD devices without a verified managed identity are refused.
security_impact: References "No device posture / endpoint health attestation" — one of its two OR-conditions — firing when managed_device_enrollment_enforced is false (T1133 External Remote Services). Without a managed-device claim, any device with valid user credentials is admitted, turning a compromised personal device into a trusted-zone foothold.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review the conditional-access / VPN-client policy and confirm a managed-device claim (Intune/Jamf/UEM compliance, or a corporate device certificate) is required and unenrolled devices are refused.
how_to_obtain.navigation: Conditional-access policy bound to VPN/bastion app -> Device claim required
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Policy references a managed-device claim or device certificate as a hard precondition; unenrolled devices denied.

how_to_obtain.instruction: From an unmanaged device with valid user credentials and MFA, attempt to establish the tunnel and confirm admission is denied for lack of a managed-device claim.
how_to_obtain.command: Attempt VPN/bastion connection from an unmanaged device with valid user MFA; expect denial at the policy enforcement point.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Authentication may succeed but the session is denied due to missing device claim; no trusted-zone reachability.

option_description: Attestation that administrative SSH/RDP into the trusted zone is mediated exclusively through the bastion / jump host — production hosts reject management connections from any non-bastion source via host firewall and network ACL, with no direct admin path that bypasses recording / JIT / mediation controls.
security_impact: References "Bastion bypass via direct admin path to backend" — its sole OR-condition — firing when bastion_mediates_all_admin_access is false (T1133 External Remote Services). Direct admin paths defeat mediation, session recording, and JIT.

how_to_obtain.instruction: From a non-bastion source on the user network, attempt ssh and rdp directly to a production host's management interface and observe filtering.
how_to_obtain.command: From a non-bastion source on the user network, attempt ssh/rdp directly to a production host's management interface.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Connection refused / filtered by host firewall and network ACL; only the bastion's source IP/identity is permitted.
how_to_obtain.source: OpenSSH bastion / jump host hardening practice

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review network ACLs / security groups for management ports (22, 3389, equivalents) on trusted-zone hosts and confirm the inbound allow-list resolves to the bastion identity only.
how_to_obtain.command: Review network ACLs / security groups for management ports on trusted-zone hosts.
how_to_obtain.navigation: Cloud console -> VPC / Security Groups -> Production tier -> Inbound rules for 22/3389
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Inbound 22/3389 (and equivalent management ports) restricted to the bastion's source identity; no broader allow-list.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect IaC / firewall change history for any temporary or emergency rules that opened management ports beyond the bastion identity and confirm they have been retired.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: No standing exceptions remain; any historical break-glass rules are removed or scoped to bastion identity.

option_description: Attests that administrative privilege on production is granted just-in-time (time-bound, approval-gated) and that no permanent/standing admin entitlements exist on production hosts or control-plane roles. Secure value is true (JIT-only, no standing admin).
security_impact: References "Standing admin privilege with no JIT and no session recording" — one of its two OR-conditions — firing when no_standing_admin_privileges_jit_required is false (T1078 Valid Accounts). Standing admin lets an attacker who phishes a user inherit durable admin power without traversing a recorded, gated path.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review PAM/IdP role memberships for production admin: confirm memberships are time-bound (TTL / approval workflow) and that no permanent human accounts hold admin.
how_to_obtain.navigation: PAM / IdP console -> Role assignments -> Production admin roles -> TTL & approval requirement
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Admin role memberships are time-bound; enumeration of production-host local admin groups returns no permanent user accounts.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Enumerate effective admin group members on a sample production host (Linux: wheel/sudo via getent; Windows: privileged AD groups) and confirm only break-glass and JIT-elevated principals appear, each with expiry.
how_to_obtain.command: getent group wheel ; getent group sudo  # Linux  -- or: Get-ADGroupMember -Identity 'Domain Admins'  # Windows
how_to_obtain.expected_output: No permanent human members; only break-glass and JIT-elevated principals present, with expiry.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Audit the JIT system's grant log: confirm grants are time-bounded, approval-gated, and revoked on expiry, with no manual extensions accumulating to de facto standing access.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Grant log shows bounded TTLs and clean expirations; no chronic re-grants approximating standing privilege.

option_description: Attests that all interactive administrative sessions traverse a PAM/bastion that records the session (keystroke, command transcript, or video) to tamper-evident storage. Secure value is true (PAM-mediated and recorded).
security_impact: References "Standing admin privilege with no JIT and no session recording" — one of its two OR-conditions — firing when privileged_access_via_pam_with_session_recording is false (T1078 Valid Accounts). Without mediation and recording, admin actions are unattributable and forensically opaque, removing the deterrent and detection value of the crossing.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm the PAM/bastion is the only ingress for interactive admin sessions and that session recording is enabled (keystroke transcript, command log, or video) to tamper-evident storage.
how_to_obtain.navigation: PAM admin console -> Recording policy -> Storage integrity
how_to_obtain.expected_output: PAM/bastion config shows recording enabled for all admin tunnels; storage is write-once or integrity-protected; retention meets policy.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Open a test admin session through the PAM/bastion and verify a recording artefact (command transcript / .cast / video) is produced and cannot be deleted by the session owner.
how_to_obtain.command: Open a test admin session; verify the recording artefact exists (command transcript / .cast / video) and that an unprivileged user cannot delete it.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Recording present, attributable to the session, immutable to the session owner.

option_description: Attests the VPN/bastion edge appliance is on a vendor-supported version and current on security patches within the organisation's SLA, with no open KEV-listed CVE applicable to the running version (e.g. CVE-2023-27997 FortiOS, CVE-2024-3400 PAN-OS, CVE-2023-46805 Ivanti Connect Secure).
security_impact: References "Unpatched / management-exposed VPN edge appliance" — one of its two OR-conditions — firing when edge_appliance_patched_within_sla is false (T1190 Exploit Public-Facing Application). Unpatched edges with KEV-listed CVEs are the canonical target for pre-auth RCE or session-token theft against the boundary itself.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Query the VPN/bastion edge appliance for its running software version and cross-check the result against vendor advisories and the CISA KEV catalog.
how_to_obtain.command: Query VPN appliance for software version; cross-check against vendor advisories / CISA KEV.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Version is supported and not affected by open KEV entries.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review the patch-management SLA for edge appliances and the change-record evidence that the running version is within SLA (critical patches inside the documented window).
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Documented SLA exists; change records show critical patches applied within the SLA window; no aged unpatched critical advisories.
how_to_obtain.source: NSA/CISA Selecting and Hardening Standards-based Remote Access VPN Solutions

option_description: Attests the VPN/bastion edge appliance's administrative / management interfaces (web-admin, SSH-admin, API console on ports such as 8443/4443/22) are not reachable from untrusted internet sources — only the VPN service ports answer on the public interface; the management plane is bound to an internal interface or jump-host network.
security_impact: References "Unpatched / management-exposed VPN edge appliance" — one of its two OR-conditions — firing when edge_management_interfaces_not_internet_reachable is false (T1190 Exploit Public-Facing Application). Internet-exposed management planes magnify the blast radius of any edge CVE.

how_to_obtain.instruction: From an internet-side host, port-scan the appliance's public IP for admin/web-admin ports (8443, 4443, 22 admin) and confirm only sanctioned VPN service ports answer.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Only sanctioned VPN service ports respond (e.g. UDP 500/4500 IPsec, UDP 51820 WireGuard, TCP 443 SSL VPN); admin/management interfaces unreachable from untrusted networks.
how_to_obtain.source: NSA/CISA Selecting and Hardening Standards-based Remote Access VPN Solutions

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect the appliance interface bindings to confirm the management plane is bound to an internal interface or jump-host network, not the public WAN interface.
how_to_obtain.navigation: Edge appliance admin console -> System -> Management access -> Interface bindings
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Management/admin services bound to internal/management interface only; public WAN interface exposes only VPN service ports.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm there is no permissive cloud security-group rule or NAT mapping that re-exposes the management plane (e.g. a hypervisor-level port-forward that bypasses the appliance interface binding).
how_to_obtain.expected_output: No SG rule or NAT mapping exposes admin ports to 0.0.0.0/0; any management access is via VPN/ZTNA or jump network.
